source.title: On the Noisy Gradient Descent that Generalizes as SGD
source.authors: Jingfeng Wu; Wen-Qing Hu; Haoyi Xiong; Jun Huan; V. Braverman; Zhan-Xing Zhu

page_placements.theme: Noise structure and finite-step dynamics affect learning conditionally

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including supplementary material, is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests the large-batch generalization gap with a compensatory sampling-noise intervention and reports held-out accuracy; this is a different intervention from the original large-batch studies.
record.gate_note: The paper compares noisy gradient descent (MSGD) with SGD and reports held-out test accuracy. Figure 1's comparisons of noise classes bear on the broader claim but do not map to a listed version, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. Cited results from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out accuracy across SGD batch sizes and tests whether compensatory sampling noise removes the resulting penalty. This bears on V5, although comparisons hold iterations fixed rather than epochs and therefore do not directly establish its fixed-epoch claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that noise class need not be crucial when magnitude and covariance are suitable, that scaled-Fisher and SGD-covariance Gaussian noises yield similar regularization, and that tuned compensatory sampling noise closes the observed large-batch gap. Their experiments do not establish recovery at matched epoch budgets.
record.recipe_differences: Adds multiplicative sampling noise or compensatory noise to gradient descent or large-batch SGD; does not test the original claim's label memorization or width interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with dataset, batch size, whether compensatory noise is added, and whether standard training tricks are used.

fits_no_version.finding: With suitable noise magnitude and covariance, several noise classes yield similar held-out accuracy. Correct SVHN Figure 1(b) values are SGD 86.00% and MSGD-Cov 85.86%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The distribution class of gradient noise need not determine its regularization effectiveness when magnitude and covariance are suitably configured.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 108 (2020)
record.problems: Figure accuracy values are endpoints without reported uncertainty. Large-batch comparisons are plotted against iteration count, and fixed-epoch equivalence is not established in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: None. Figure 1 noise-class comparisons were retained as rows linked to fits_no_version; other Figure 1 algorithm endpoints are not separately extracted because the paper's prose describes their close performance but they do not add a listed-version result.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and paired natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.

Matched epoch budgets, including recovery within the same epoch budget; language models; workload-dependent batch thresholds; controlled tests of longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, or normalization and regularization changes. Large batches process more examples at matched iterations, and ghost batch normalization is already used for large-batch ResNet training.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing memorized examples versus randomly selected examples.

missing.what: VGG-11 CIFAR-10 batch sweep and compensatory-noise recovery: SGD-100 77.34%, SGD-1k 73.92%, SGD-5k 71.24%; mini-batch MSGD-Fisher at 1k/5k 78.68%/78.34%; mini-batch MSGD-Cov at 1k/5k 78.76%/78.85%. Uses no batch normalization, augmentation, or weight decay and an iteration-based schedule.
missing.locator: Supplement C.4, Figure 4(b), and C.3 optimization setup

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. Comparisons use iteration-based schedules, so their V5 evidence is conditional on that budget. Figure endpoints and Table 1 report no uncertainty; small differences should not be interpreted as established improvements.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

The paper reports large-batch comparisons and compensatory-noise results, but does not establish a fixed-epoch comparison. It does not test longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, or normalization and regularization changes as gap-closing interventions.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.

relation.reason: The study reports its own small-versus-large-batch accuracy comparisons and tests compensatory noise, rather than merely citing or assuming the penalty.

tranche.reason: Different noise interventions directly investigate the large-batch generalization penalty and its recovery. The comparisons address V5 under iteration budgets without establishing matched-epoch behavior.
